questions.stem: A company wants application servers to read objects from a storage bucket without embedding long-lived credentials in the application. Which TWO actions together meet this requirement?
options: Attach an identity role to the server instances that grants read access to the bucket.
Store an access key in a configuration file on each server.
Grant the bucket's read permission to the role rather than to a user.
Rotate the embedded access key every 90 days.
questions.explanation: Instance roles provide short-lived credentials automatically; granting the bucket permission to that role completes the design. Embedded keys, even rotated, are what the requirement rules out, and a public bucket exposes the data to everyone.

questions.stem: Which of the following encrypts data at rest in block storage with the LEAST operational effort?
options: Provider-managed encryption enabled on the volume.
Application-level encryption of every file before write.
A third-party encryption appliance in front of the volume.
Manual encryption of snapshots after they are taken.
questions.explanation: Provider-managed volume encryption is a single setting with no key handling in the application or operations path.
